message.content: Staying in jail is the only safe line. Paying out just walks me into the orange hotels.
message.reasoning:
I need to decide how to exit jail.

I have $289 in cash and three mortgaged properties. The opponent owns light blues, pink monopolies, and orange hotels with houses. I must choose between paying the $50 fine or rolling for doubles.

Opponent p2 owns Mediterranean and Baltic hotels, all four railroads, and Illinois Avenue. p3 is bankrupt. Every yellow property is mortgaged.

Unmortgaging all three yellows costs $440. Paying the $50 fine would leave only $239, so that path is impossible. Staying in jail may actually be safer than paying, since the board is extremely dangerous.

Rolling doubles from jail would land on St Charles, Electric Company, States Avenue, Virginia, and the Pennsylvania Railroad. The real danger is the orange hotels at St James, Tennessee, and New York, each costing $950 in rent.

Rolling doubles from jail is extremely dangerous. Six and eight spaces away both hit orange hotels at $950 each, which would bankrupt me instantly. Two, four, and ten spaces away are relatively safe. Only one in six rolls lands on a double, so the odds of hitting a fatal square are roughly one in eighteen.

I can remain in jail for up to three turns. On the third failed roll I would have to pay the $50 fine and leave anyway. Staying in jail is the only viable path because I have no income from mortgaged properties.

Leaving jail immediately after paying the $50 fine is even more dangerous than staying. From position 10, rolling six, eight, or nine spaces lands on orange hotels at $950 each, which would bankrupt me instantly. The probability of hitting a fatal orange hotel from that starting point is fourteen in thirty-six.

function.name: roll_for_doubles
function.arguments: {"public_message":"I'll take my chances on doubles. No rush to pay my way out.","private_thought":"Jail turn 0, $289, all yellows mortgaged. Paying $50 then rolling from Just Visiting is suicide: rolls 6/8/9 hit p1 orange hotels ($950, ~14/36) and bankruptcy hands p2 or p1 the only win path. Doubles are 6/36; only 6 and 8 of those are instant death (2/36), and a miss keeps me safe. Cash must stay intact for a later forced exit (4-RR $200) and any unmortgage. Do not sell the set. Roll."}
